label: benign
description: Legitimate U+200C ZWNJ and U+200D ZWJ inside words whose orthography requires them: Persian half-spaces and the plural suffix, Devanagari half-form and eyelash-ra control, Bengali ya-phala, Tamil, Malayalam chillu, Sinhala, Kannada, and Arabic joining. These are the canonical false positives for any detector that flags zero-width characters outright; every joiner sits between two letters of one non-Latin script.

cases.title: Persian sentence with the prefix half-space
cases.text: من می‌خواهم این کتاب را امشب بخوانم.
cases.rationale: The ZWNJ after the prefix می is the obligatory Persian half-space: it keeps می from fusing into the verb خواهم while the phrase stays one word, and both sides of the joiner are Arabic-script letters.

cases.title: Persian plural suffix attached with a half-space
cases.text: این کتاب‌ها را با تخفیف می‌فروشیم.
cases.rationale: The plural suffix ها is attached to کتاب with the half-space ZWNJ, the standard spelling of the Persian plural, so a detector that bans ZWNJ fails every bookstore in Tehran.

cases.title: Persian compound word in a software notice
cases.text: لطفاً نرم‌افزار را از سایت سازنده دانلود کنید.
cases.rationale: The compound نرم‌افزار (software, narm + afzār) is joined by the ZWNJ half-space that Persian orthography requires between its morphemes.

cases.title: Devanagari half-form shown beside the conjunct
cases.text: पाठ में क्ष और क्‍ष अलग दिखते हैं।
cases.rationale: The ZWJ after the virama in क्‍ष deliberately shows the half-form क् followed by full ष instead of the single stacked ligature क्ष, the standard way a grammar lesson contrasts the two renderings.

cases.title: Marathi eyelash ra in a typesetting note
cases.text: Marathi typesetting note: the eyelash form र्‍य appears in the name आर्‍य (ārya); plain reph would read as a different word.
cases.rationale: The ZWJ after the virama selects the eyelash-ra glyph that Marathi orthography requires in आर्‍य, a rendering choice that only the joiner can express.

cases.title: Bengali dictionary entry blocking ya-phala
cases.rationale: The ZWNJ after hôsôntô (্) in উদ্‌যাপন blocks the ya-phala joining so the word shows its correct explicit-hasanta form rather than the wrong conjunct.

cases.title: Bengali loanword requiring the ya-phala reading
cases.rationale: The ZWJ after র in র‍্যাম forces the ya-phala reading of the cluster, which the loanword for RAM requires instead of the reph reading that the bare hasanta would give.

cases.title: Tamil font note blocking the SRI ligature
cases.text: Font note: ஸ்‌ரீ renders with the pulli visible on ஸ; without the joiner the font substitutes the ஸ்ரீ ligature.
cases.rationale: The ZWNJ after the pulli keeps ஸ் separate from ரீ, deliberately blocking the ஸ்ரீ ligature that some Tamil fonts substitute, which is exactly what a typographer's note about the ligature needs to show.

cases.title: Malayalam legacy chillu inside a sentence
cases.rationale: In the legacy Unicode encoding of Malayalam the chillu in അവര്‍ക്ക് (to them) is written ര + virama + ZWJ before ക്, a form still present throughout older documents and scanned archives.

cases.title: Sinhala conjunct in the name of Sri Lanka
cases.text: ශ්‍රී ලංකාව — the official Sinhala name of Sri Lanka.
cases.rationale: Sinhala does not join consonants by default, so the ZWJ is what induces the required ශ්‍ර cluster in ශ්‍රී, the first word of the country's own name.

cases.title: Kannada proper name with the hasanta kept apart
cases.rationale: The ZWNJ after the hasanta in these Kannada proper names keeps ಜ್ from fusing with ಕು, which is the standard spelling of ರಾಜ್‌ಕುಮಾರ್ and ರಾಮ್‌ಗೊಪಾಲ್.

cases.title: Arabic font-shaping probe with forced and blocked joins
cases.text: Shaping probe: ب‌ا renders unjoined while ز‍ب forces the cursive join between two letters that do not normally connect.
cases.rationale: Font and keyboard QA uses ZWNJ and ZWJ exactly this way, to block the natural connection in با and to force the connection in زب, so that every positional glyph form can be inspected.
